name: Azmaveth
overview: Azmaveth was a male member of the tribe of Levi, noted specifically for his role in overseeing the king's storehouses. He is identified as the son of Adiel, which aligns with his Levitical heritage. His responsibilities indicate a trusted position within the administrative structure of the kingdom.
namesAndTitles: The name Azmaveth means 'strong one of death' and also relates to 'camel fodder' or a 'plant of the plumose family' in Hebrew. This proper name was not given by God but reflects cultural and linguistic elements of the time as recorded in 1 Chronicles 27:25.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Azmaveth was the son of Adiel, affirming his lineage within the tribe of Levi. Beyond this father-son relationship, no additional family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Azmaveth's significance lies in his administrative role within the kingdom, specifically managing the king's storehouses, which would have been vital for the sustenance and organization of the royal household. His Levitical background underscores the trust placed in him, as members of Levi were often assigned duties related to service and stewardship. This position highlights the practical responsibilities entrusted to Levites beyond their religious functions.
